resources.string: Hibernates apps by opening their App info page and pressing Force stop, when fast mode is not available. Also presses Allow on the wireless debugging prompt right after Hibernate turned wireless debugging on. Only sees Settings and that prompt.
Hibernate uses accessibility to press Force stop when fast mode is not available, and to answer the wireless debugging prompt after a reboot. Turn on Hibernate in Accessibility settings.
Launched since they were last stopped. Apps at the top will be hibernated; tap an app for options.
Stopped: they only wake up when you open them, or when something else starts them.
These apps could not be stopped last time.
Set up fast mode or turn on accessibility
Turn on Hibernate in Accessibility settings, or set up fast mode.
Could not hibernate: turn on accessibility or set up fast mode
Fast mode failed (%1$s); used accessibility instead.
Preinstalled apps with an icon in the app drawer. Background services are never touched.
Hibernate only the apps you pick, instead of every awake app.

Always kept awake: the keyboard, the home screen, phone and messaging apps, accessibility services, apps with notification access, the live wallpaper and device admins. Stopping those would break them until you open them again.
Hibernate when the screen turns off
After the screen has been off for the delay below. In accessibility mode the screen turns on dimmed and dark while it works, then off again.
Turning the screen back on before this cancels it.
Stops apps instantly through the phone\'s own wireless debugging, with nothing on screen. Needs Wi-Fi; otherwise accessibility mode is used.
Only if Hibernate turned it on.
Covers the Settings pages while Hibernate goes through them.
Raise it if some apps fail on a slow phone.
Your lists and options, as a small JSON file.
With \"Only my list\" on, only these apps are hibernated.
These apps are always left awake.
Fast mode uses the phone\'s own wireless debugging, like a computer running adb, but from inside Hibernate and only on this phone. It needs a one-time setup from a computer with adb and a USB cable.
1. Allow Hibernate to switch wireless debugging
adb shell pm grant com.unl0cker.hibernate android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
Run this on the computer, then tap Authorize. The phone asks \"Allow USB debugging?\": tick \"Always allow from this computer\" and tap Allow. The fingerprint shown is Hibernate\'s own key.
Waiting for you to tap Allow on the phone…
Already done: Hibernate is authorized and fast mode has worked. Nothing to do here.
Hibernate is already authorized, so there is nothing to approve. Run \"Test fast mode\" below to check it. To authorize again anyway, run adb tcpip 5555 on the computer first.
adb is not waiting on port 5555 yet. Run adb tcpip 5555 on the computer, then tap Authorize again.
Authorized and tested: fast mode works. adb is back in USB mode.
This key was already authorized, so the phone did not need to ask. Fast mode works; adb is back in USB mode.
Authorized, and adb is back in USB mode. Connect to Wi-Fi and run the test to confirm.
This key was already authorized, so the phone did not need to ask. adb is back in USB mode.
The phone allowed Hibernate only once and did not keep its key. Run adb tcpip 5555 again, tap Authorize, and tick \"Always allow from this computer\" before tapping Allow.

Turns wireless debugging on (Wi-Fi needed), connects and runs a harmless command. After a reboot, Android 11 and 12 ask once more whether to allow wireless debugging on the network; Hibernate answers Allow by itself while accessibility is on.
The phone did not keep Hibernate\'s key. Run step 2 again and tick \"Always allow from this computer\" before tapping Allow.
Needed to answer the wireless debugging prompt after a reboot, and as the fallback without Wi-Fi.
